subject: Renewal: Add reserved GPUs & hardware-class uplift (A100 -> H100) — perf/$ analysis
messages:
From: Vince Marshall <vince@acmeai.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmeai.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — reserved GPUs and perf/$ question

Dev —

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. We’re approaching our renewal for the dedicated pool (current: 16x A100 reserved) and the exec team asked two clear questions before we sign: 1) if we move to H100s (or L40S variants), what is the realistic throughput uplift for our RLHF-heavy inference workloads, and 2) what’s the expected performance-per-dollar when we include license/commit pricing over a 12-month term?

Procurement also wants the draft amendment so they can start internal approvals. Can you send a short techno-economic note + the proposed amendment showing incremental cost and guarantees?

Thanks,
Vince
Vince Marshall
Head of ML Platforms, AcmeAI

---

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: Vince Marshall <vince@acmeai.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, Procurement <procurement@acmeai.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 12:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — reserved GPUs and perf/$ question

Hi Vince —

Appreciate the quick summary. I put together a concise analysis and a draft amendment for Procurement attached. High level:

- Measured uplift: for your typical RLHF inference mix (batch size=1-4, seq len ~1k, KV-cache reuse ~40%), H100s deliver ~2.6x median tokens/sec vs A100 in our dedicated runtime; L40S options are ~2.1x but cheaper per-GPU.
- Performance-per-dollar (12-month committed pricing, includes reserved pool discount): moving to H100s improves effective cost-per-token by ~15–22% after factoring in throughput and reduced queue times. The L40S path often gives similar dollar throughput at lower absolute commit due to better price/GPU but slightly lower latency headroom.
- Throughput guarantees: we can extend your SLA to include a committed baseline of 12k tokens/sec sustained per pool with burst policy. For the requested commit increase (from 16 -> 24 GPUs equivalent), we propose: 18 H100 reserved + 6 L40S burst capacity, 99.95% availability on baseline, and an automatic fallback to A100-compatible variants in rare capacity constraints.

Attachments: redwood_h100_tco_model_v2.xlsx (workbook with per-workload sims), commit_amend_draft_v3.docx (legal-friendly amendment).

Next steps I suggest:
- Lauren to confirm pricing band and margin-sensitive discounts (cc’d)
- Soojin to validate SLA language and failover clause
- Vince / Procurement to review and confirm acceptance or redlines

I’m flexible on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk the spreadsheet.

Best,
Dev Patel
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

---

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Vince Marshall <vince@acmeai.com>, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, Procurement <procurement@acmeai.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — reserved GPUs and perf/$ question

Vince / Procurement team —

Quick clarifications on pricing and commercial structure:

- Pricing bands: 12–24 H100 reserved GPUs: list $5,100/GPU-month; tiered discount brings effective price to $3,570–$4,080/GPU-month depending on term and commit.
- Mix model proposed (18 H100 + 6 L40S) yields a blended effective GPU-month price that is competitive with your current A100 spend while improving throughput. The attached workbook models three scenarios (A100-rollover, H100-upgrade, H100+L40S hybrid).
- For a 12-month commit we can offer a one-time onboarding credit of $30k applied to month 1 and a 6% price protection clause if cloud rates in your region change >10%.
- SLA language: Soojin will propose explicit throughput guarantee language (tokens/sec baseline + degraded-mode fallbacks). Latency SLOs remain best-effort for burst above baseline.

If Procurement is comfortable I can push the amendment to legal for final edits. Otherwise we can do a short call and resolve redlines.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

---

From: Elena Rossi <elena@acmeai.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, Vince Marshall <vince@acmeai.com>, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 16:41:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — reserved GPUs and perf/$ question

Team —

Thanks for the materials. Procurement reviewed the amendment and has two small asks: 1) can the onboarding credit be moved to a pro-rated rebate over the first three months instead of a lump sum, and 2) can we add a short acceptance test (5 business days) after initial provisioning to validate the throughput numbers against our production prompt set? We’ll sign after those two items are reflected.

Vince asked me to push the Docs to our legal e-sign today; he’ll confirm if he prefers DocuSign or internal e-sign.

Elena Rossi
Procurement Manager, AcmeAI
